name: Shechem
overview: Shechem was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, identified specifically as the son of Gilead. He is noted in Scripture in connection with the Shechemites, a group named after him, indicating his significance within his tribal context. His identity is primarily grounded in his lineage and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Shechem means 'shoulders and upper part of the back,' or possibly 'shoulder' as in the saddle of a hill. This proper name, not given by God, reflects a geographical or physical characteristic, which is consistent with biblical naming practices of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Shechem was the son of Gilead. Beyond this, there are no additional family relationships noted in the biblical text concerning Shechem.
scriptureSignificance: Shechem's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a tribal figure within Manasseh and as the eponymous ancestor of the Shechemites. This connection highlights the importance of lineage and tribal identity in Israel's history and the preservation of God's covenant people. His mention underscores the detailed genealogical records that Scripture maintains to affirm God's providential care over His chosen tribes.
